title: Critical/Minor Ambiguity: Server-Sent Events MUST return event.data
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

I reviewed the [Server-Sent Event specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html) and there is a critical ambiguity causing a lot of problems. The error event seems oriented around connectivity issues, _not_ HTTP responses.

Currently browsers are intentionally dropping the `event.data` object _just_ because the server did not respond with an HTTP 200 response. If the server responds, there is no network connectivity issue. That `event.data` contains information about the error.

This leads to developers having to choose from the following:

1. Intentionally sabotage the appropriate server response to the client to get the error message via `event.data`.
2. Make a redundant request to a RAM wasting string that shouldn't exist to get the client the error message.
3. Leave the bug caused by browsers as-in to the detriment of the client, developer and the owner of the website.

None of these scenarios are acceptable.

Therefore it's necessary to address this ambiguity at the specification level so we can get the browser vendors to correct this bug and ensure developers and users get the appropriate outcome.

### Passing Specification Update
A short snippet to visualize what complying with the updated specification looks like:

```
es.example = new EventSource(event_source_url);

es.example.onerror = function(event)
{
 console.log('this must be returned for onerror though currently is not:', event.data);
}
```
